ENV-01.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same floating shelf of dark rock 40 m wide and 56 m long with a ragged asymmetric outline, about 6 m thick at the rim and tapering into an inverted cone 48 m deep with a faint bronze vein glowing inside it, six thick rusted chains hanging from bronze rim rings into the haze. At the near end is the SPAWN TERRACE, an irregular paved patch about 13 x 9 m of cracked slabs of different sizes, with a shallow bronze arrival disc (3.6 m across, three concentric rings, slightly sunken and cracked) at its centre and a low broken rock lip behind it; a tiny plain 1.8 m human silhouette stands on the disc facing the door in every view for scale. A broken road of uneven worn slabs about 4 m wide, with a thin broken bronze inlay line, leads about 11 m to THE BEAM: one colossal weathered bronze I-girder 16 m long with a 2.5 m wide top, lying slightly crooked (about 15 degrees off the straight line) across a ragged meandering crack that cuts the whole island from rim to rim, 8 to 11 m wide with stepped broken lips and a 60 m drop into haze; the beam is level but dented, rust-streaked, matte, dusty, with missing rivets and a chipped corner, never polished. Beyond it a broken irregular forecourt about 13 x 4 m, then three worn uneven steps rising to THE DOOR, shown LOCKED, cut into the face of a huge black rock cliff with raw rock on both sides: 8 m high, carved stone frame 7.6 m wide with a crown of bronze finials, battered green-bronze verdigris scrollwork leaves dark with soot, two thick rusted chains wound across both leaves held by one huge closed padlock, a thin bright amber line of light through the centre gap, exactly like the Core Fantasy key-art door. Behind the door the cliff holds a walkable antechamber: a 3 m passage, then an irregular carved hall about 16 x 11.5 m with an 11 m cracked ceiling, four stout columns (two whole, two broken) around a clear aisle, a low round dais 4.5 m across where three weapons hover, completely dark inside with no daylight (only the faint glow of the weapons), a small west alcove, and, at the east side of the hall, a short flight of 5 wide worn stone steps going DOWN into a 4 m opening (the exit tunnel) in the east wall that leads out onto a rock ledge on the cliffs east face where a fixed bridge leaves toward the next island. The door sits low at the foot of ONE enormous, deep, solid mountain of black-brown fractured rock that rises 36 m at its west shoulder and 60 m at its summit, as thick and heavy as it is tall, with a huge cave carved inside it. The whole mass is built from countless big rough boulders, slabs, ribs and buttresses piled and jammed together, so the area around the door is crowded with many large rocks and ledges, with broken scree at their feet. Its upper part splits into two high crooked peaks (60 m and a 36 m one leaning west), which are simply the top of the same mass, not separate objects. All one rock: NO windows, NO openings, NO bricks or cut stone, NO tiers, NO battlements, NO carvings, nothing built. Only a faint amber glow deep in a few natural cracks. Around the base stand six chunky broken rock outcrops of 20 to 48 m, different heights, thick at the base, blunt snapped tops, NOT needles, NOT cones, NOT icicles. NO masonry on them: no bricks or courses of cut stone, no battlements, no crenellations, no arched windows, no columns, no domes, no bands or carved panels, nothing that looks built, Roman or medieval. Three bare dead trees (6 m, 4.5 m, and a 2.8 m broken stump) stand off the road, a few small uneven clumps of dry grass, and rubble in uneven scatters of different-sized stones; no mirror symmetry anywhere, immense, silent and ominous; match the attached approved ENV-01 hero image and blueprint sheets exactly, and add no second floating island or extra rock in the background, shown from 6 angles in one image, arranged in a clean grid (front, back, left side, right side, top, underside). Every view must be the exact same object with identical design, proportions and scale, rendered with neutral even studio lighting and no shadows hiding detail, no scene, no camera tilt. A large bold title banner at the top reading exactly "ENV-01 - STARTING SHELF ISLAND" with a smaller size note "~40 x 56 m" beside it, and a small label under each view with the angle name; all text short, high-contrast, spelled correctly, each label appears only once. Every island must have a dramatically unique, instantly recognizable grand silhouette with one signature feature, immense sense of scale, mysterious ancient engineered ruins, deep volumetric haze and warm rim light, interesting to look at from every angle. Match the approved key art: weathered sandstone-tan and dark charcoal-brown layered rock with obsidian-black shards, warm gold-amber dusty haze light, photoreal cinematic game-asset concept, rough eroded surfaces with sharp fractured edges, sparse dry dead fossil-like trees and thin dry grass tufts only. REAL, NOT A TOY: photoreal massive geology and ancient ruined architecture, as if photographed at full size. Heavy erosion, soot, dust, deep cracks, spalled and chipped stone, rust and verdigris streaks, irregular asymmetric forms. NOT a toy, NOT a miniature or diorama or snow-globe, NOT smooth clay or plastic, NO tidy repeating wedding-cake tiers, NO cute rounded domes, no cartoon proportions, no flat even colour. Matte grimy materials, one low warm sun, deep shadows, strong rim light. NATURAL, NOT STAGED: nothing stands alone like a prop on a table; every structure is grown out of, carved into or half-buried in the rock, bases merged with scree, rubble and fallen blocks. Irregular organic outlines, uneven ground, off-centre and overlapping forms, no neat rows, no mirror symmetry, one obvious focal point. Ruins, NOT a city, no skyscrapers, no glass, no modern architecture, no green lush vegetation.

ENV-03.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same medium floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 30 m wide, with a ragged uneven outline and a heavy rough underside. Along its north edge rises ONE GRAND MASSIF of natural rock: huge, thick and monumental, like a small mountain range or the great rock buttes of a canyon land, and like the tall rock clusters in the approved key art. It is a single mass that grows out of the island with no gaps at its base. It has a very wide heavy base about 22 m wide, and out of it rise five or six enormous crags of very different heights. TOWERING is the point. The crags are like the great spires of the Dolomites, the basalt pillars of Zhangjiajie and the fractured slate peaks of a mountain range, only crooked and leaning. THE BIGGEST CRAG RISES ABOUT TWICE AS HIGH AS THE WHOLE ISLAND IS WIDE (about 55 m on a 30 m island), so in the front view it is far taller than the island is long, and the island looks small beneath it. The second crag is about 38 m, then 34 m, 26 m, 18 m and 12 m, so the skyline is a jagged crown of very different heights: one extra tall spire, two or three tall ones, then medium ones and low broken shoulders. Do NOT make them all the same height. Every crag is thick at the base and rises in a long tapering shape, narrowing unevenly toward a ragged broken top, with long vertical fluting and deep vertical cracks, big ledges, overhangs and collapsed notches, wind grooves and thin lighter brown seams. They stand as ONE TIGHT OVERLAPPING CLUSTER, NOT in a fan, NOT in a row, NOT side by side like the fingers of a hand: some crags in front, some behind, two leaning against each other, one leaning out over the hollow, each leaning 10 to 25 degrees at a different angle, tops broken and jagged, the tallest off to the left of centre. They are fused at the base into one wide heavy mass with lower rock buttresses and stepped shoulders, with a few fallen boulders at the foot. They are NOT short blunt boulders, NOT squat blocks, NOT thin slabs, NOT planks, NOT fins, NOT ribs, NOT teeth, NOT stacked blocks, NOT toy bricks, NOT a neat row of equal stones, NOT like fingers, and NOT icicles or cones. In front of the crags the top dips into a small sheltered hollow with a plain flat floor of bare dark rock with nothing lying on it, thin straight bronze lines inlaid in the floor leading to one short stone column on a round bronze base with a small dark fire bowl on top, unlit. There are no steps, no stairs and no platforms. On the west edge a thin plank-and-chain bridge arrives at a short bronze socket post, and on the east edge a short fixed stone bridge end with a second short bronze socket post leaves toward the next place. At the south-east edge, away from the crags, a big flat-topped natural boulder with a worn smooth top sits right on the rim, facing the open sky. Nobody sits on it. ENV-04.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same large floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 60 m wide, with sheer broken cliff faces all around, a ragged oval outline, and a deep underside like an upside-down mountain of fractured rock with a few long hanging rock tendrils and a faint bronze vein deep in the cracks. In the middle of the top is one DEEP CRATER, about 30 m across and 18 m deep, with sheer cracked rock walls and three broad broken ledges stepping down to a flat floor far below. The crater is an irregular oval, NOT round, NOT neat rings, NOT a stadium, NOT a quarry with tidy steps. Thin amber light glows faintly in the cracks of the crater floor and walls, dim and dormant, like a sleeping reservoir of energy. Thin straight bronze lines are inlaid in the crater floor. SHOW (fill the frame with this and nothing else): one long broad flight of broken uneven rock steps cut into the dark mountain face, wide enough for several people, one thin bronze line down its middle, a sheer drop into haze on the outer side, the next landing above, close up.
WHERE IT IS: a part of the Summit Peak Island, a HUGE tiered mountain peak of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, floating in open sky above the clouds. One broad path of broken, uneven rock steps zigzags up its face in five long flights joined by four flat landings, with one thin bronze line down the middle. Near the top a wide flat crown of cracked dark rock with one short stone column on a round bronze base. Two tall natural rock spires lean together like a gate where the path reaches the crown. Behind the crown a steep stair of broken dark rock steps with six small dark unlit bronze braziers leads to a higher broad flat terrace where the colossal black volcanic Throne of Stillness stands (about 40 m tall, a very tall narrow backrest with six faint horizontal amber fissures and two arching bronze dragon ribs), with two huge natural rock spires at the foot of the stair. Dry and dead, no green, no grass, no trees. NO props. Nothing else is built.
ATTACH: the sheet, both blueprint pictures, the ENV-06 sheet (for the rock style) and the THR-01 Throne sheet. Match their design, materials and wear. ORIENTATION: the arrival ledge at the foot is on the LEFT (west).
LOOK: photoreal, real size, not a toy. Rough, worn and uneven, never smooth or tidy or symmetrical. Matte, grimy materials. Warm gold-amber light with deep shadows. Do not write any numbers or notes in the picture.
TITLE: a bold title bar at the top that reads exactly "ENV-07 - SUMMIT PEAK ISLAND - DETAIL 1: FLIGHT OF ROCK STEPS". Spell it correctly. Show it only once.

ENV-08.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same chain of FIVE separate floating rock masses (two cliffs and three shelves) of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 285 m long in all, with wide gaps of open sky and a deep drop into cloud between them, loosely staggered and NOT in a straight row: a big West Cliff about 70 m long where the player arrives, a small South shelf south of the line, a Middle shelf south-east of it, a North shelf a little north of the line, and a huge East Cliff, the biggest, about 86 m long; the West Cliff and the East Cliff are the two halves of one split mountain, each with sheer vertical faces carrying the same five horizontal bands of thin lighter brown strata at the same heights, so the bands line up across the whole chain as though the mountain was torn apart; flat cracked broken tops; each mass hangs over a short thick tapering root of rough rock wreathed in cloud; three short bridges cross three of the gaps (West Cliff to South shelf, South shelf to Middle shelf, North shelf to East Cliff), each made of two heavy dark chains strung between two short bronze posts on a flat rock tongue at each side, with flat rungs of which only the first four at the near end glow amber-white; one narrow natural rock ridge as wide as a path joins the Middle shelf to the North shelf; one very long bridge of the same kind crosses from the West Cliff straight to the North shelf; ONE short stone column on a round bronze base on the East Cliff; a wide flat lip at the north-east corner of the East Cliff with faint heat shimmer rising and two low natural rock needles beside it; a cluster of three black natural rock needles of different heights on the north rim of the West Cliff; a round shallow hollow in the top of each of the West Cliff and the three shelves. Nothing is built. Dry and dead, no green, shown from 4 angles in one image, arranged in a clean grid (front, back, top, underside). Every view must be the exact same object with identical design, proportions and scale, rendered with neutral even studio lighting and no shadows hiding detail, no scene, no camera tilt. A large bold title banner at the top reading exactly "ENV-08 - CANYON CLIFFS" with a smaller size note "chain ~285 m long: five rock masses, four bridges and the Spine" beside it, and a small label under each view with the angle name; all text short, high-contrast, spelled correctly, each label appears only once. Irregular organic outlines, uneven ground, off-centre and overlapping forms, no neat rows, no mirror symmetry, one obvious focal point. No city, no glass, no green lush vegetation. On the north rim of the West Cliff a cluster of three black natural rock needles of different heights. A round shallow hollow in the top of the West Cliff and of each of the three shelves. THE WORLD BEFORE THE BREAK: Igara is ONE ENORMOUS FLOATING ISLAND, a flying continent, huge, green, safe and full of life, not an archipelago and not broken. Vast green hills, forests, meadows, lakes and terraced farmland on top, waterfalls pouring off the edges into a sea of cloud, a mighty natural underside of dark layered rock. Homes are advanced and graceful, NOT square and NOT medieval: smooth curved organic sci-fi dwellings built INSIDE the rock cliffs, rounded and oval windows lit warm amber from inside, carved curved balconies and ledges, arched openings, vertical gardens, soft curved bronze and pale stone surfaces, like apartments grown into the cliff. No square boxes, no pitched tile roofs, no timber cottages. The sky is full of advanced curved flying craft (smooth teardrop and ring-shaped skycraft with warm amber fire-drives), floating lanterns, small floating garden pods and many birds. Photoreal cinematic game concept, soft gold-amber dawn light, warm and hopeful, rich greens against dark rock. No skyscrapers, no glass towers, no neon, no jets or modern airliners, no religious imagery, no readable text except the labels. SHAPE: NOT a tidy disc, oval or single block. An irregular, asymmetrical, leaning landmass: one long twisting tail of land, deep bays and inlets, a great natural rock arch you can see through, a high ridge on one side and a low sunken valley on the other, with a few small green islets and rock fragments trailing close beside it, joined by hanging roots and thin veils of falling water. The underside is a ragged forest of long rock spires and hanging roots of very different lengths. OTHER WORLDS: Igara is not alone. Around it float many other islands of every size and shape: three or four mid-size wild green neighbours at different distances, a scatter of small rock islets, and far in the haze a huge pale planet with a ring and a smaller moon. They are wild and empty, no buildings, only trees and waterfalls, so Igara reads as the one inhabited home. WATER: it must make sense. A thick permanent bank of cloud is caught against the high peak and ridge; it rains and snow-melts there, feeding a crater lake near the summit. From the lake, streams run down the hills through the terraces, fill the lower lakes, and spill over the rim as waterfalls. Below the rim every waterfall breaks into mist, and the mist rises on warm updrafts through the sea of cloud and climbs back to the peak: a closed cycle you can see. GREEN: forests and meadows grow in a deep blanket of dark soil that sits on the rock top, thickest along the streams and lakes. Great roots and vines grip the cliff edges and hang down the sides, and the greenest ground follows the water. SUN: a low gold sun is half risen out of the cloud-sea horizon, behind and to one side of the island, so the whole island is backlit with a bright rim light, long soft shadows fall across the hills, shafts of light cut through the mist and the waterfalls glow. The sea of cloud below reflects warm gold light up onto the rock underside. The island turns very slowly, so the same sun sets back into the cloud sea on the far side at dusk. WATER SYSTEM: tall bronze cloud-catcher fins and net-sails on the ridge beside the Throne pull moisture from the cloud bank into a summit reservoir and crater lake; stone-lined channels and short aqueducts carry it down through the terraces to lower lakes; the surplus spills over the rim at a few controlled waterfalls whose mist rises on updrafts back to the ridge. SAFETY: all walkways, terraces and the skyport rim have solid waist-high curved bronze railings or low stone walls and the island rim has a continuous guard wall. Craft are skycraft: smooth discs with a glass dome and a glowing amber ring. Only a few people anywhere, never a crowd.

Still from an Oscar-winning Hollywood live-action film, large-format cinema camera, photographic realism, real skin and fabric, lighting and palette as described in the scene. Spaceships are manta-ray shaped skycraft, organic, never round. Small clean labels with thin leader lines reading exactly: "Igara", "Skyport", "Throne", "Six lines of fire", "Dragon", "Skycraft", "Ringed planet", "Summit lake". PT-001.long: A single cinematic 16:9 widescreen storyboard frame, photoreal game-cinematic concept art. Epic wide establishing shot at dawn, the fixed hero view from the south and slightly above, slow drift. The whole of Igara before the break at dawn, from the hero view, the island filling the middle of the picture. The Throne stands on the mountain with the six bars of fire above it. Skycraft glide in and out along the skyport trailing thin amber light, and a very few tiny people walk the skyport deck behind its rail. A living, organic, bronze-green Dragon glides high in the sky at the upper left with its wings spread and no fire on it. A huge pale ringed planet and two small moons fill the upper right. The low gold sun rises at the far right horizon, backlighting the clouds with long soft rays; floating amber lanterns and flocks of birds fill the air, and mist from the waterfalls rises back up through the clouds. Beautiful, peaceful, vast. Design notes: the whole of Igara before the break: ONE enormous irregular, asymmetrical green floating island with a twisting tail, bays and a rock arch, rock-carved dwellings, a skyport and many flying craft, surrounded by many smaller wild floating islands and a distant ringed planet, with a cloud-fed lake, streams and waterfalls that turn to mist and rise again; the Skyport of Igara, a long slender S-curved platform deck hewn from the island's natural rock along the right rim, ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins, with a gallery of arched openings and hangar mouths below the deck; the Throne, about 40 m tall, standing on the highest rocky peak of the great island at the very top of the world, reached by one long carved staircase, hewn from black volcanic stone and bronze, a deep seat with two thick armrests, a very tall narrow monolith backrest with six equally spaced horizontal fissures, two colossal curved bronze dragon ribs arching inward on both sides, molten-amber cracks, a long steep staircase of broken black stone with bronze braziers on both sides, never modern, glossy or floating, a plain dark monolith and NOT a castle, NOT a gothic spire, with no towers or pointed turrets; the six sky lines, six long straight horizontal glowing bars, evenly spaced and parallel, stacked like a ladder, never stars or circles. Labelled storyboard: add small clean engraved-bronze callout labels with thin amber leader lines, each pointing at its subject and reading exactly: "Igara", "Skyport", "Throne", "Six lines of fire", "Dragon", "Skycraft", "Ringed planet", "Summit lake". EXACT LOOK OF WHAT APPEARS IN THIS FRAME (draw each one exactly like this, and nothing else of the world beyond what the camera sees): THE ISLAND (the same shape in every picture, never redesigned): ONE enormous floating island of green land about 3 km long, a long horizontal slab seen from the front at its fixed hero view (the camera stands to the south, slightly above, so the island runs left to right across the picture: left end = west, right end = east). It is widest in the middle, with a blunt rounded left end and a long slender curving tail on the right. A high cliff of warm grey-brown layered rock forms its front, with two tiers of rock-carved homes; its underside is a ragged mass of long jagged rock spires, deepest below the middle. LEFT END: a great natural rock arch, a thick curved bridge of rock that you can see through, with a small waterfall beneath it into a blue bay, beside a large blue lake along the left rim whose water spills over the rim in a tall waterfall. Behind that lake on the back ridge sits a small round summit lake ringed by a crescent of tall, thin, curved, sail-shaped cloud-catcher fins of pale bronze. CENTRE: one steep rounded green mountain, the highest hill, with the Throne on its summit and one straight staircase of black stone with burning braziers coming down its right face; terraced fields in strips of green and gold on the front slope, a short stone aqueduct and channel running to a pool at the front rim, and waterfalls pouring over the front rim in three places. RIGHT: the skyport, a long slender S-curved platform deck that runs out along the rim from the foot of the mountain to the far right tip, ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins, with a natural rock arch beneath it. Fixed in every picture: arch and lake at the left, mountain and Throne in the middle, skyport at the right. It floats in a sea of soft white-blue cloud, with a few small wild floating islands around it. Thin gold veins of fire glow faintly in the hanging rock underneath. THE THRONE: it stands alone on the very top of the highest green hill in the middle of the island and never anywhere else. It is a single plain monolith about 40 m tall: a tall narrow slab of black volcanic stone with a slightly tapering rectangular body and a flat top, six thin horizontal glowing amber fissures evenly spaced up its face, two huge curved polished bronze ribs arching inward around its base like a pair of horns, and one long steep staircase of broken black stone with small bronze braziers climbing the hill straight up to its foot. Plain monolith, not a castle, no turrets, no windows, no spire. THE SIX LINES OF FIRE: EXACTLY SIX long, perfectly straight horizontal bars of glowing gold fire, counted one, two, three, four, five, six, all exactly the same length, thin like glowing rods with a white-gold core and a soft orange glow, evenly spaced with equal dark gaps, perfectly parallel and stacked vertically like the rungs of a ladder with six rungs. They float alone in open sky directly above the Throne, together about a third as tall as the island, the lowest bar a little above the top of the Throne. Six bars, always six. THE DRAGON: a great living creature about 60 m long with a long graceful neck, a long tail, four legs tucked under its body and two broad leathery bat-like wings with visible veins, covered in smooth dark bronze-green scales with a paler cream belly and warm calm amber eyes. It glides slowly with wings spread. It looks like a living animal, with no flame, no smoke, no glow and no cracks on it. THE SKYCRAFT: brand-new, very advanced spaceships, each about 15 m long, shaped like a manta ray: a wide swept-back delta wing with two long pointed wingtips curving slightly downward, a slim raised central fuselage with a long dark tinted canopy, and a tapering tail. The hull is smooth matte dark graphite-grey with a hint of green; thin glowing amber-orange light lines trace the edges of the wings and the canopy and small amber vents sit on the wings. Sleek, minimal and futuristic: never a round disc, no dome, no wheels, no jet engines. They glide in a few lines in and out of the skyport with a short trail of amber light. THE SKYPORT: a long slender S-curved platform deck, about 600 m long, hewn out of the island's own natural rock, running out along the right rim from the foot of the mountain to the far right tip and ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins and a ring of lit windows. TOP DECK: a broad curving landing deck with rows of small glowing amber guide-lights set into it, where a few skycraft rest at docking fins and a few tiny travellers walk behind the rail. BELOW IT: a curved gallery of tall arched openings carved into the cliff, glowing warm amber, and rounded hangar mouths from which skycraft launch, with a natural rock arch beneath the deck. A low carved-rock guard wall with a slim bronze rail runs along every deck edge, and people stay behind it. Moss, trees and small gardens grow along its edges. EXACT LOOK OF WHAT APPEARS IN THIS FRAME (draw each one exactly like this, and nothing else of the world beyond what the camera sees): THE ISLAND (the same shape in every picture, never redesigned): ONE enormous floating island of green land about 3 km long, a long horizontal slab seen from the front at its fixed hero view (the camera stands to the south, slightly above, so the island runs left to right across the picture: left end = west, right end = east). It is widest in the middle, with a blunt rounded left end and a long slender curving tail on the right. A high cliff of warm grey-brown layered rock forms its front, with two tiers of rock-carved homes; its underside is a ragged mass of long jagged rock spires, deepest below the middle. LEFT END: a great natural rock arch, a thick curved bridge of rock that you can see through, with a small waterfall beneath it into a blue bay, beside a large blue lake along the left rim whose water spills over the rim in a tall waterfall. Behind that lake on the back ridge sits a small round summit lake ringed by a crescent of tall, thin, curved, sail-shaped cloud-catcher fins of pale bronze. CENTRE: one steep rounded green mountain, the highest hill, with the Throne on its summit and one straight staircase of black stone with burning braziers coming down its right face; terraced fields in strips of green and gold on the front slope, a short stone aqueduct and channel running to a pool at the front rim, and waterfalls pouring over the front rim in three places. RIGHT: the skyport, a long slender S-curved platform deck that runs out along the rim from the foot of the mountain to the far right tip, ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins, with a natural rock arch beneath it. Fixed in every picture: arch and lake at the left, mountain and Throne in the middle, skyport at the right. It floats in a sea of soft white-blue cloud, with a few small wild floating islands around it. Thin gold veins of fire glow faintly in the hanging rock underneath. THE THRONE: it stands alone on the very top of the highest green hill in the middle of the island and never anywhere else. It is a single plain monolith about 40 m tall: a tall narrow slab of black volcanic stone with a slightly tapering rectangular body and a flat top, six thin horizontal glowing amber fissures evenly spaced up its face, two huge curved polished bronze ribs arching inward around its base like a pair of horns, and one long steep staircase of broken black stone with small bronze braziers climbing the hill straight up to its foot. Plain monolith, not a castle, no turrets, no windows, no spire. THE SIX LINES OF FIRE: EXACTLY SIX long, perfectly straight horizontal bars of glowing gold fire, counted one, two, three, four, five, six, all exactly the same length, thin like glowing rods with a white-gold core and a soft orange glow, evenly spaced with equal dark gaps, perfectly parallel and stacked vertically like the rungs of a ladder with six rungs. They float alone in open sky directly above the Throne, together about a third as tall as the island, the lowest bar a little above the top of the Throne. Six bars, always six. THE EYE: a huge almond-shaped eye that is part of the sky and made of the SAME living gold-white energy as the six lines of fire and the veins in the rock, not a drawn symbol and not a physical eye. About as wide as the whole island, hanging high above the six lines. Its outline is not a hard line: it is formed by sweeping banks of cloud lit with gold along their edges and fine glowing filaments that fade into the real clouds, so clouds pass in front of and behind it. The iris is a great round disc of warm gold-white filaments like sun rays, the same colour and glow as the six bars, and the filaments of the iris reach down and join the top bar, so the Eye and the six lines read as one single living system of energy. The pupil is a narrow vertical diamond of deep dusk-blue sky with a few faint stars, translucent, never solid black. The iris is turned down toward the island and the Throne: awake, calm, kind and watching over the people, never angry. No eyelids, no lashes, no skin, no wet surface, no flames, no lightning. Only the eye, no face, no body. THE SKYCRAFT: brand-new, very advanced spaceships, each about 15 m long, shaped like a manta ray: a wide swept-back delta wing with two long pointed wingtips curving slightly downward, a slim raised central fuselage with a long dark tinted canopy, and a tapering tail. The hull is smooth matte dark graphite-grey with a hint of green; thin glowing amber-orange light lines trace the edges of the wings and the canopy and small amber vents sit on the wings. Sleek, minimal and futuristic: never a round disc, no dome, no wheels, no jet engines. They glide in a few lines in and out of the skyport with a short trail of amber light. THE SKYPORT: a long slender S-curved platform deck, about 600 m long, hewn out of the island's own natural rock, running out along the right rim from the foot of the mountain to the far right tip and ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins and a ring of lit windows. TOP DECK: a broad curving landing deck with rows of small glowing amber guide-lights set into it, where a few skycraft rest at docking fins and a few tiny travellers walk behind the rail. BELOW IT: a curved gallery of tall arched openings carved into the cliff, glowing warm amber, and rounded hangar mouths from which skycraft launch, with a natural rock arch beneath the deck. A low carved-rock guard wall with a slim bronze rail runs along every deck edge, and people stay behind it. Moss, trees and small gardens grow along its edges. Never a round or ring-shaped structure, never a separate building, no glass dome. THE HOMES: advanced curved homes carved INSIDE the natural rock cliff itself, as if the rock were hollowed out: the rough, weathered, mid-brown and warm grey rock stays the dominant material and wraps every opening, with tall rounded oval windows and arched doorways glowing warm amber from inside, curved rock galleries and balconies with hanging green vines and small lanterns, bronze used only as thin trim. Nothing is a separate building attached to the rock, no square windows, no flat boxes, no pitched roofs, no glass or metal facades. THE GREEN: rich natural colour: deep forest-green dense tree canopies, bright yellow-green meadows, terraced fields in strips of lighter green and gold, small orange-flowering vines, all growing in dark brown soil on top of the rock and richest along the water; hanging vines and roots drape the cliff edges. Plain monolith, not a castle, no turrets, no windows, no spire. THE SIX LINES OF FIRE: EXACTLY SIX long, perfectly straight horizontal bars of glowing gold fire, counted one, two, three, four, five, six, all exactly the same length, thin like glowing rods with a white-gold core and a soft orange glow, evenly spaced with equal dark gaps, perfectly parallel and stacked vertically like the rungs of a ladder with six rungs. They float alone in open sky directly above the Throne, together about a third as tall as the island, the lowest bar a little above the top of the Throne. Six bars, always six. THE HOMES: advanced curved homes carved INSIDE the natural rock cliff itself, as if the rock were hollowed out: the rough, weathered, mid-brown and warm grey rock stays the dominant material and wraps every opening, with tall rounded oval windows and arched doorways glowing warm amber from inside, curved rock galleries and balconies with hanging green vines and small lanterns, bronze used only as thin trim. THE GREEN: rich natural colour: deep forest-green dense tree canopies, bright yellow-green meadows, terraced fields in strips of lighter green and gold, small orange-flowering vines, all growing in dark brown soil on top of the rock and richest along the water; hanging vines and roots drape the cliff edges. On the top deck six docking arms reach out over the drop, each cradling a parked skycraft; two skycraft lift off and one comes in to land, trailing ribbons of amber light. In the middle gallery a few travellers, five or six at most, walk behind the bronze railings: a woman with a small child, an old man with a staff, two people carrying bundles. PT-007.sheet: Cinematic 16:9 widescreen storyboard frame, photoreal. Very wide shot from high above Igara, looking out across the sky. Igara on the left, and the six lines above its Throne. From it, faint threads of pale gold light stretch across the sky, and manta-ray skycraft glide along them in single file, each carrying a few small bronze lanterns. In the distance on the right are two neighbour worlds: Maren, a cluster of small reef-like floating islands with tall white sail-fins and blue-green water terraces, and Sol, a ring of floating garden islands with orchard terraces of dark green and bronze-gold fruit trees. Above Igara, the calm Eye watches the lanes. A sea of cloud, morning light. Characters and places: THE EYE: a huge almond-shaped eye formed out of the sky itself, not a physical eye: made entirely of soft glowing energy and light-haze, translucent and blended into the clouds so it reads as part of the atmosphere. About as wide as the whole island. The almond outline is only a faint pale cloud-light halo that merges into the clouds; in the middle sits a bright round iris of warm amber-gold light made of fine radial strands like sun rays, and at its centre a narrow vertical diamond-shaped pupil, deep brown-black like a window into deeper sky. The iris is turned downward toward the island and the Throne: it is awake, attentive and watching over the people, the vast presence of a great unseen being of which we see only this eye, calm and kind, never angry. Faint thin filaments of light fade away into the clouds. Clouds drift in front of and behind it so it never looks like a sticker. No eyelids, no lashes, no skin, no veins, no wet surface, no flames, no lightning, no sparks. Only the eye, no face, no body. Still from an Oscar-winning Hollywood live-action film, large-format cinema camera, photographic realism, real skin and fabric, lighting and palette as described in the scene. People are fair, European-looking, bare-headed, calm faces, in premium tailored stone-grey, silver-grey, beige or taupe clothes (long open coat-robe over fitted tunic, fitted high-necked bodysuit with ankle boots, or long high-collared gown), no two alike, never poor clothes; at most 6 people, children 2 or 3 at most. Spaceships are manta-ray shaped skycraft, organic, never round. Small clean labels with thin leader lines reading exactly: "Igara", "Maren", "Sol", "Sky lane", "The Eye". Thin black header strip: "Movie: Before" at top-left, "The Sky Lanes" at top-right; thin black footer strip reading "PT-007 - THE SKY LANES". No other text. EXACT LOOK OF WHAT APPEARS IN THIS FRAME (draw each one exactly like this, and nothing else of the world beyond what the camera sees): THE ISLAND (the same shape in every picture, never redesigned): ONE enormous floating island of green land about 3 km long, a long horizontal slab seen from the front at its fixed hero view (the camera stands to the south, slightly above, so the island runs left to right across the picture: left end = west, right end = east). It is widest in the middle, with a blunt rounded left end and a long slender curving tail on the right. A high cliff of warm grey-brown layered rock forms its front, with two tiers of rock-carved homes; its underside is a ragged mass of long jagged rock spires, deepest below the middle. LEFT END: a great natural rock arch, a thick curved bridge of rock that you can see through, with a small waterfall beneath it into a blue bay, beside a large blue lake along the left rim whose water spills over the rim in a tall waterfall. Behind that lake on the back ridge sits a small round summit lake ringed by a crescent of tall, thin, curved, sail-shaped cloud-catcher fins of pale bronze. CENTRE: one steep rounded green mountain, the highest hill, with the Throne on its summit and one straight staircase of black stone with burning braziers coming down its right face; terraced fields in strips of green and gold on the front slope, a short stone aqueduct and channel running to a pool at the front rim, and waterfalls pouring over the front rim in three places. RIGHT: the skyport, a long slender S-curved platform deck that runs out along the rim from the foot of the mountain to the far right tip, ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins, with a natural rock arch beneath it. Fixed in every picture: arch and lake at the left, mountain and Throne in the middle, skyport at the right. It floats in a sea of soft white-blue cloud, with a few small wild floating islands around it. Thin gold veins of fire glow faintly in the hanging rock underneath. THE THRONE: it stands alone on the very top of the highest green hill in the middle of the island and never anywhere else. It is a single plain monolith about 40 m tall: a tall narrow slab of black volcanic stone with a slightly tapering rectangular body and a flat top, six thin horizontal glowing amber fissures evenly spaced up its face, two huge curved polished bronze ribs arching inward around its base like a pair of horns, and one long steep staircase of broken black stone with small bronze braziers climbing the hill straight up to its foot. Plain monolith, not a castle, no turrets, no windows, no spire. THE SIX LINES OF FIRE: EXACTLY SIX long, perfectly straight horizontal bars of glowing gold fire, counted one, two, three, four, five, six, all exactly the same length, thin like glowing rods with a white-gold core and a soft orange glow, evenly spaced with equal dark gaps, perfectly parallel and stacked vertically like the rungs of a ladder with six rungs. They float alone in open sky directly above the Throne, together about a third as tall as the island, the lowest bar a little above the top of the Throne. Six bars, always six. THE EYE: a huge almond-shaped eye that is part of the sky and made of the SAME living gold-white energy as the six lines of fire and the veins in the rock, not a drawn symbol and not a physical eye. About as wide as the whole island, hanging high above the six lines. Its outline is not a hard line: it is formed by sweeping banks of cloud lit with gold along their edges and fine glowing filaments that fade into the real clouds, so clouds pass in front of and behind it. The iris is a great round disc of warm gold-white filaments like sun rays, the same colour and glow as the six bars, and the filaments of the iris reach down and join the top bar, so the Eye and the six lines read as one single living system of energy. The pupil is a narrow vertical diamond of deep dusk-blue sky with a few faint stars, translucent, never solid black. The iris is turned down toward the island and the Throne: awake, calm, kind and watching over the people, never angry. No eyelids, no lashes, no skin, no wet surface, no flames, no lightning. Only the eye, no face, no body. The hull is smooth matte dark graphite-grey with a hint of green; thin glowing amber-orange light lines trace the edges of the wings and the canopy and small amber vents sit on the wings. Sleek, minimal and futuristic: never a round disc, no dome, no wheels, no jet engines. They glide in a few lines in and out of the skyport with a short trail of amber light. THE GREEN: rich natural colour: deep forest-green dense tree canopies, bright yellow-green meadows, terraced fields in strips of lighter green and gold, small orange-flowering vines, all growing in dark brown soil on top of the rock and richest along the water; hanging vines and roots drape the cliff edges. THE WATER SYSTEM: clear blue-green lakes and a winding river; a small summit lake high on the ridge just below the Throne's hill, fed by the cloud catchers: six to eight tall thin curved sail-shaped fins of pale bronze and translucent membrane standing in an arc on the ridge around the Throne's hill, pulling moisture out of the cloud bank; stone-lined channels and a short stone aqueduct carry the water down through the terraces to the lower lakes; the surplus pours off the rim in several long white waterfalls whose mist drifts down into the cloud sea and is lifted back up by warm air. SAFETY: every walkway, terrace, balcony, bridge and the skyport rim has a continuous waist-high curved bronze guard rail or a low stone wall, and the island's outer rim has a guard wall; people stay well inside the railings and nobody stands at or over an open edge. At dusk by the window the Mother kneels beside her son and tells him the old story, her hand on his chest. Beside them on the wall a child's chalk drawing of a turtle with six lines on its shell. The boy is listening with his whole face. The parents' faces are never clearly seen in this scene: shown from behind, in deep shadow, in profile against the light, or only as hands and shoulders. His face is visible. Design notes: Elias as a boy of nine, small and slight, fair European-looking skin with a few light freckles, a soft round face with a small straight nose and large calm dark-brown watchful eyes, short tousled dark-brown hair, a tailored fitted high-collared tunic in fine soft grey-beige wool with a slim belt, slim tailored trousers and polished soft dark boots, clearly well-to-do and cared for; the Mother, a woman in her thirties, calm and kind, fair European-looking skin, an oval face with soft smile lines and gentle hazel-brown eyes, long dark-brown hair tied back at the nape with a thin gold thread, a long fitted high-collared dress in soft taupe-grey with a small bronze clasp at the shoulder and a long beige scarf over her shoulders. EXACT LOOK OF WHAT APPEARS IN THIS FRAME (draw each one exactly like this, and nothing else of the world beyond what the camera sees): THE SIX LINES OF FIRE: EXACTLY SIX long, perfectly straight horizontal bars of glowing gold fire, counted one, two, three, four, five, six, all exactly the same length, thin like glowing rods with a white-gold core and a soft orange glow, evenly spaced with equal dark gaps, perfectly parallel and stacked vertically like the rungs of a ladder with six rungs. They float alone in open sky directly above the Throne, together about a third as tall as the island, the lowest bar a little above the top of the Throne. Six bars, always six. THE HOMES: advanced curved homes carved INSIDE the natural rock cliff itself, as if the rock were hollowed out: the rough, weathered, mid-brown and warm grey rock stays the dominant material and wraps every opening, with tall rounded oval windows and arched doorways glowing warm amber from inside, curved rock galleries and balconies with hanging green vines and small lanterns, bronze used only as thin trim. Nothing is a separate building attached to the rock, no square windows, no flat boxes, no pitched roofs, no glass or metal facades. PT-022.sheet: Cinematic 16:9 widescreen storyboard frame, photoreal. Wide shot of the sky, slow push. The six lines of fire flicker and dim one by one, the Eye half closed, the pale blue sky with gold only near the sun draining to grey. Birds settle on rooftops. The whole world seems to hold its breath. Soft grey-amber light, long shadows, melancholy but not scary. Characters and places: THE EYE: a huge almond-shaped eye formed out of the sky itself, not a physical eye: made entirely of soft glowing energy and light-haze, translucent and blended into the clouds so it reads as part of the atmosphere. About as wide as the whole island. The almond outline is only a faint pale cloud-light halo that merges into the clouds; in the middle sits a bright round iris of warm amber-gold light made of fine radial strands like sun rays, and at its centre a narrow vertical diamond-shaped pupil, deep brown-black like a window into deeper sky. The iris is turned downward toward the island and the Throne: it is awake, attentive and watching over the people, the vast presence of a great unseen being of which we see only this eye, calm and kind, never angry. Faint thin filaments of light fade away into the clouds. Clouds drift in front of and behind it so it never looks like a sticker. No eyelids, no lashes, no skin, no veins, no wet surface, no flames, no lightning, no sparks. Only the eye, no face, no body. Still from an Oscar-winning Hollywood live-action film, large-format cinema camera, photographic realism, real skin and fabric, lighting and palette as described in the scene. People are fair, European-looking, bare-headed, calm faces, in premium tailored stone-grey, silver-grey, beige or taupe clothes (long open coat-robe over fitted tunic, fitted high-necked bodysuit with ankle boots, or long high-collared gown), no two alike, never poor clothes; at most 6 people, children 2 or 3 at most. Spaceships are manta-ray shaped skycraft, organic, never round. Small clean labels with thin leader lines reading exactly: "Six lines dimming", "Eye". Thin black header strip: "Movie: The Quiet Season" at top-left, "The Fire Goes Quiet" at top-right; thin black footer strip reading "PT-022 - THE FIRE GOES QUIET". No other text. At the far right end, on the long S-curved skyport deck, a second even smaller figure, the boy in a grey-beige tunic, runs along the deck toward the foot of the staircase. PT-034.sheet: Cinematic 16:9 widescreen storyboard frame, photoreal. Wide aerial shot, brilliant. A huge column of white-gold light erupts from the Throne and fills the sky, the six lines blazing all at once brighter than ever, birds exploding upward, the whole world lit like noon. For one beat it is the most beautiful thing ever seen. It is widest in the middle, with a blunt rounded left end and a long slender curving tail on the right. A high cliff of warm grey-brown layered rock forms its front, with two tiers of rock-carved homes; its underside is a ragged mass of long jagged rock spires, deepest below the middle. LEFT END: a great natural rock arch, a thick curved bridge of rock that you can see through, with a small waterfall beneath it into a blue bay, beside a large blue lake along the left rim whose water spills over the rim in a tall waterfall. CENTRE: one steep rounded green mountain, the highest hill, with the Throne on its summit and one straight staircase of black stone with burning braziers coming down its right face; terraced fields in strips of green and gold on the front slope, a short stone aqueduct and channel running to a pool at the front rim, and waterfalls pouring over the front rim in three places. RIGHT: the skyport, a long slender S-curved platform deck that runs out along the rim from the foot of the mountain to the far right tip, ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins, with a natural rock arch beneath it. Fixed in every picture: arch and lake at the left, mountain and Throne in the middle, skyport at the right. Design notes: the whole of Igara before the break: ONE enormous irregular, asymmetrical green floating island with a twisting tail, bays and a rock arch, rock-carved dwellings, a skyport and many flying craft, surrounded by many smaller wild floating islands and a distant ringed planet, with a cloud-fed lake, streams and waterfalls that turn to mist and rise again. Labelled storyboard: add small clean engraved-bronze callout labels with thin amber leader lines, each pointing at its subject and reading exactly: "Igara breaking". EXACT LOOK OF WHAT APPEARS IN THIS FRAME (draw each one exactly like this, and nothing else of the world beyond what the camera sees): THE ISLAND (the same shape in every picture, never redesigned): ONE enormous floating island of green land about 3 km long, a long horizontal slab seen from the front at its fixed hero view (the camera stands to the south, slightly above, so the island runs left to right across the picture: left end = west, right end = east). It is widest in the middle, with a blunt rounded left end and a long slender curving tail on the right. A high cliff of warm grey-brown layered rock forms its front, with two tiers of rock-carved homes; its underside is a ragged mass of long jagged rock spires, deepest below the middle. LEFT END: a great natural rock arch, a thick curved bridge of rock that you can see through, with a small waterfall beneath it into a blue bay, beside a large blue lake along the left rim whose water spills over the rim in a tall waterfall. Behind that lake on the back ridge sits a small round summit lake ringed by a crescent of tall, thin, curved, sail-shaped cloud-catcher fins of pale bronze. CENTRE: one steep rounded green mountain, the highest hill, with the Throne on its summit and one straight staircase of black stone with burning braziers coming down its right face; terraced fields in strips of green and gold on the front slope, a short stone aqueduct and channel running to a pool at the front rim, and waterfalls pouring over the front rim in three places. RIGHT: the skyport, a long slender S-curved platform deck that runs out along the rim from the foot of the mountain to the far right tip, ending in one slim bronze control spire with swept docking fins, with a natural rock arch beneath it. Fixed in every picture: arch and lake at the left, mountain and Throne in the middle, skyport at the right. It floats in a sea of soft white-blue cloud, with a few small wild floating islands around it. Thin gold veins of fire glow faintly in the hanging rock underneath. THE SKYCRAFT: brand-new, very advanced spaceships, each about 15 m long, shaped like a manta ray: a wide swept-back delta wing with two long pointed wingtips curving slightly downward, a slim raised central fuselage with a long dark tinted canopy, and a tapering tail. The hull is smooth matte dark graphite-grey with a hint of green; thin glowing amber-orange light lines trace the edges of the wings and the canopy and small amber vents sit on the wings. Sleek, minimal and futuristic: never a round disc, no dome, no wheels, no jet engines. They glide in a few lines in and out of the skyport with a short trail of amber light. THE GREEN: rich natural colour: deep forest-green dense tree canopies, bright yellow-green meadows, terraced fields in strips of lighter green and gold, small orange-flowering vines, all growing in dark brown soil on top of the rock and richest along the water; hanging vines and roots drape the cliff edges. THE WATER SYSTEM: clear blue-green lakes and a winding river; a small summit lake high on the ridge just below the Throne's hill, fed by the cloud catchers: six to eight tall thin curved sail-shaped fins of pale bronze and translucent membrane standing in an arc on the ridge around the Throne's hill, pulling moisture out of the cloud bank; stone-lined channels and a short stone aqueduct carry the water down through the terraces to the lower lakes; the surplus pours off the rim in several long white waterfalls whose mist drifts down into the cloud sea and is lifted back up by warm air. SAFETY: every walkway, terrace, balcony, bridge and the skyport rim has a continuous waist-high curved bronze guard rail or a low stone wall, and the island's outer rim has a guard wall; people stay well inside the railings and nobody stands at or over an open edge. THE VEINS OF FIRE: thin, warm gold veins of light, like glowing roots, run from the base of the Throne down through the natural rock of the whole island, under the hills, along the cliffs and beneath the terraces and lakes, pulsing very slowly and gently in time with the six lines, as if the island were breathing. They are calm and soft, never blinding, and the island stays green and healthy. PEOPLE: only a very small handful, at most 6, each clearly drawn, never a crowd. PT-060.sheet: Cinematic 16:9 widescreen storyboard frame, photoreal. ELIAS IS COMPLETELY ALONE: he is the only person in the whole picture. Extreme wide view from just behind and above the Starting Shelf in the south-west, looking north-east up the whole climb. Island positions, sizes, spacing and heights as described, in the exact look of the game's key art: warm gold-amber cinematic dusk, dark bronze-lit stone, a sea of clouds, photoreal. THE FEELING: this is a world far too big and too complex to finish in an hour, and the goal is not visible yet. It is a SHATTERED WORLD, not a path: a whole planet was blown apart and the ten numbered islands are only the biggest surviving pieces. Fill the frame with wreckage at every depth: torn rock shards and slabs in the foreground, colossal broken crust plates hanging far behind, a few shards cracked with molten amber. The numbered islands stay the largest and best lit so a first climb can be read, but the route is long, indirect and mostly unseen. THE GOAL IS HIDDEN: the Throne spire at the top left is almost lost in layers of haze and distant shards, only a faint thin dark spire with a tiny amber glint, so the player cannot yet tell where the climb ends. Every island carries tall dark ruined bronze-lit towers and spires, as in the references: tapering tower ruins with sheared tops on the plateau (5), capped drum towers and one needle spire on the arena (7), twin towers with a broken arch on the canyon (8), a gatehouse tower on the summit stair, with glowing amber lanterns on the tallest. Where there is a gap between islands, the crossing is a RUNG BRIDGE: two chains with glowing amber horizontal bars as rungs, exactly like the glowing bars of the six lines, as in The Leap reference; some gaps have no bridge at all. Not a plank-and-rope bridge. In the foreground, step 1, the dark cracked Starting Shelf with its bronze ring disc and two lantern posts, very large in the lower frame, and the tiny Elias with the Cinder at its edge looking up. Clearly BELOW the Eye and never hidden by it, the six sky lines hang large and separate as six long glowing amber bars, each one wider than the biggest island, as in the Summit reference. The RING OF FIRE: a vast thin ring of dormant fire encircles the whole world far away on the horizon, a line of smouldering embers and low dark flames curving around everything, so its enormous size shows. It is not yet ignited, it only smoulders, and it is the proof of how large the world is. The Fire Dragon is MASSIVE and unmissable, as in the Flying reference: a huge winged dragon with dark bronze-black scales, wings spread wide and veined with molten amber, banking in side view across the upper middle of the frame, trailing sparks. Two LARGE planets fill the sky, as in the references: a huge ringed planet and a huge cracked glowing ember planet, both partly hazed. Warm low sun, long rim light on the towers, layered haze so each island is hazier than the last. Only the labels listed below. Soft gold-amber haze, warm light on the high spire, the lowest tiers in cooler shadow. Characters and places: the world is NOT flat: it is a six-tier climb of broken floating islands at rising heights. The Starting Shelf is the lowest island at the lower left. Beside it a small twisted stepping island and a medium island with a windbreak ridge. Then a field of drifting moving platforms rising to a large plateau, a circular arena to the east, a canyon cliff pair far to the north-east, a drifting cluster of fragments across the north, and the highest point of all, a slender summit spire crowned by the Throne at the upper left. Every tier sits higher than the last, with cloud seas below and between them. The distances are vast: the Throne is about 700 m from the start, roughly seventeen widths of the Starting Shelf, and about 360 m higher, so from island 1 it is a tiny spire at the far horizon with ten islands and wide gaps of cloud and void between; the gaps are as wide as or wider than the islands, the bridges are long thin threads and some gaps have no bridge at all, only drifting slabs; the Starting Shelf Island: a ragged floating shelf of dark rock, an irregular cracked spawn terrace with the sunken bronze arrival disc where the player appears, a broken worn road to a crooked weathered bronze beam lying across a jagged meandering crack, a broken forecourt and three worn steps to the locked door cut into a huge black cliff with one enormous deep mountain of boulder rock (36 m shoulder, 60 m summit, two high peaks of the same mass) of the same dark rock growing out of it, no masonry, thick rusted chains hanging from bronze rim rings, bare dead trees and dry grass. Elias's expression stays calm, composed and restrained, at most a very faint soft look, never a broad smile or grin. WORLD RULES: this is a broken sky-world of dark floating rock islands above a sea of cloud; there is no ocean, no sea horizon, no beach, no water, no Greek or classical columns, no gothic or Victorian buildings; any ruins are tall dark bronze-lit tapering towers carved from the same dark rock. The Cinder is always a head-sized floating faceted polyhedron with a gold-bronze frame, glass-like facets and a glowing ember core, never a rock, never a spaceship. The six sky lines are exactly six straight horizontal bars of equal length stacked above one another like a ladder, never vertical, never curved, never comet streaks; before the awakening they are dark and unlit. The Eye in the sky is calm and dormant: an almond-shaped eye woven from thin pale-gold energy threads in the cloud, a soft cloud-edged outline, a gold filament iris, a translucent dusk-blue diamond pupil; no flames, no lightning, no sparks, not red, not black, not a burning eye. Still from an Oscar-winning Hollywood live-action film, large-format cinema camera, photographic realism, real skin and fabric, lighting and palette as described in the scene. Only one human figure appears in the frame, Elias. Spaceships are manta-ray shaped skycraft, organic, never round. Thin black header strip: "Island 1: Arrival" at top-left, "The World Is a Climb" at top-right; thin black footer strip reading "PT-060 - THE WORLD IS A CLIMB". No other text. TIME OF DAY: cold blue pre-dawn turning pale gold at the horizon. STORY BEAT (when and what is happening): Map · The whole climb.
